reading.title: Nudges: When Polite Wording Changes Behaviour
reading.intro_zh: 本文改编自权威行为科学机构 The Decision Lab 的案例研究，介绍英国“行为洞察小组”如何通过改写税务提醒信的措辞——而非加重处罚——显著提高纳税合规率。它和课文一样说明：礼貌而清晰的表达，往往比冷冰冰的命令更有效。

source.title: How normative messaging increased tax compliance by 15%

passage: Governments have long assumed that the surest way to make citizens follow a rule is to threaten them with a penalty. Behavioural scientists, however, argue that the precise wording of an official request can matter just as much as the fine attached to it. This insight lies at the heart of "nudge theory," popularised by Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein, who showed that small, carefully designed changes in how a choice is presented can steer people toward a desired behaviour without removing their freedom to decide. A nudge persuades rather than commands.

A striking demonstration came from the United Kingdom's Behavioural Insights Team, an advisory unit nicknamed the "Nudge Unit." Working with the national tax authority, the team rewrote ordinary reminder letters sent to people who had not yet paid. Rather than emphasising threats, the most effective version simply stated that nine out of ten people in the UK pay their tax on time, leaving the reader in an uncomfortable minority. Letters that referred to the recipient's own neighbourhood proved even more persuasive, raising compliance by roughly fifteen per cent.

The mechanism behind this success is the power of descriptive social norms: when we learn what most others around us actually do, we feel a subtle pressure to conform. The financial consequences were considerable, with millions of pounds in overdue tax collected far sooner than expected, all without harsher punishments. The lesson extends well beyond taxation. Whether on a parking notice, a hospital appointment slip, or a classroom rule, a message that is courteous, specific, and grounded in what reasonable people already do is often far more compelling than a stern warning.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Heavier fines are the only reliable way to make citizens obey the law.
How a request is worded can influence behaviour as much as the penalties behind it.
Tax authorities should stop sending reminder letters altogether.
Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein invented the modern income tax.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文主旨是：官方请求的措辞方式（“轻推”）可以像处罚一样有效地影响人们的行为，而不必依赖更重的惩罚。

questions.question: According to the passage, what did the most effective reminder letter emphasise?
options: That late payers would immediately be taken to court.
That the tax rate had recently been lowered.
That nine out of ten people in the UK pay their tax on time.
That the recipient could ignore the letter without consequences.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中指出最有效的信件强调“英国十分之九的人都按时纳税”，把未缴税者置于少数人之列。

questions.question: Why does telling people what most others do increase compliance?
options: Because it triggers descriptive social norms, creating pressure to conform with the majority.
Because it removes any legal obligation to pay.
Because it offers a cash reward to everyone who replies.
Because it makes the rule itself unclear and easy to ignore.
questions.explanation_zh: 文章解释其机制是“描述性社会规范”：当人们得知周围多数人怎么做时，会产生一种与多数人保持一致的微妙压力。

questions.question: What can be inferred about the author's view of nudges?
options: Nudges work only for collecting taxes and nothing else.
Nudges are a form of punishment disguised as politeness.
Nudges should always replace every law and regulation.
Polite, well-designed wording can be a practical tool in many everyday situations.
questions.explanation_zh: 末段把这一原理推广到停车通知、医院预约、课堂规则等场景，可推断作者认为礼貌而精心设计的措辞在许多日常情境中都是实用工具。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "compelling" most nearly means
options: persuasive and hard to resist
expensive and time-consuming
confusing and poorly written
optional and easily ignored
questions.explanation_zh: compelling 在文中指“有说服力、令人难以抗拒”，与上文说礼貌而具体的信息比严厉警告更有效相呼应。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 16 的五个核心表达提升到 B2+ 难度：用 if...will 写规则与后果，用 lucky if 写条件，用 does not always happen 做转折，用 pay attention to 提醒注意，用 cannot fail to 写“礼貌却有效”的结论。尽量把句子放进更抽象、更正式的语境里。

patterns.title: If you ..., ... will ...
patterns.source: If you park your car in the wrong place, a traffic policeman will soon find it.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 if 给出条件，用 will 写自然会发生的结果，适合说明规则和后果。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：描述一种公共政策、提醒方式或沟通策略的条件与可预期结果，语境要比校园例子更抽象正式。
patterns.sample: If you frame an official request as a polite reminder rather than a threat, ordinary citizens will usually comply far more willingly.
patterns.tip_zh: If you 后面接现在时动作；另一半用 will 写结果，不要把 will 放进 if 从句里。

patterns.title: You will be very lucky if ...
patterns.source: You will be very lucky if he lets you go without a ticket.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式强调“如果某件好事发生，你就很幸运”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写在某个充满不确定的局面里，如果某件难得的好结果真的发生，你会非常幸运。
must_include: You will be very lucky if
patterns.sample: You will be very lucky if a single carefully worded sentence persuades thousands of reluctant people to change their long-standing habits.
patterns.tip_zh: if 后面写具体条件，比如 gives you another chance / lets you try again。

patterns.title: This does not always happen
patterns.source: However, this does not always happen.
patterns.focus_zh: 用这句话把“通常会这样”转到“但并不总是这样”，很适合制造故事转折。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：先陈述一个被普遍认为理所当然的结果，再指出在现实中它并不总是会发生。
patterns.sample: Stricter penalties are widely expected to guarantee obedience, yet this does not always happen in real behavioural experiments.
patterns.tip_zh: 前一句可以写大家预期的结果；这一句负责把故事拐向例外。

patterns.title: pay attention to ...
patterns.source: You will enjoy your stay here if you pay attention to our street signs.
patterns.focus_zh: pay attention to 用来提醒别人认真看、认真听或认真注意某个规则。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：提醒读者认真注意某个抽象但重要的细节，例如措辞、语气、规则的设计或数据背后的含义。
patterns.sample: Effective policymakers pay attention to the precise wording of a message, because subtle phrasing can quietly reshape how people behave.
patterns.tip_zh: to 后面接名词或名词短语，比如 signs, rules, instructions。

patterns.title: cannot fail to ...
patterns.source: You cannot fail to obey it!
patterns.focus_zh: cannot fail to 表示“肯定会、很难不”，语气比 will 更有结论感。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：描述一个表达得既礼貌又清晰的信息，因而读者一定会理解、认同或遵从，语境尽量抽象。
patterns.sample: Once a reminder is courteous, specific, and rooted in what most reasonable people already do, you cannot fail to recognise its quiet persuasive power.
patterns.tip_zh: 这个结构有点正式，适合放在故事结尾，强调提醒真的有效。
